subproblem.title: Conjugation by a linear isometry: projections onto rotated subspaces and invariance of hsNormSq
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers and q a linear isometry equivalence of R^(n+l); write Q and Q' for q and q^(-1) = q.symm as continuous linear maps of R^(n+l). (a) For every linear subspace K of R^(n+l), the orthogonal projection onto q(K) = K.map q equals Q o p_K o Q', where p_K is the orthogonal projection onto K. (b) For every continuous linear X : R^(n+l) -> R^(n+l), hsNormSq (Q o X o Q') = hsNormSq X (Hilbert-Schmidt norm squared, computed in the standard basis).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (q : Amb n ℓ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Amb n ℓ), (∀ K : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), (K.map q.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap).starProjection = q.toLinearIsometry.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L K.starProjection ∘L q.symm.toLinearIsometry.toContinuousLinearMap) ∧ ∀ X : Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ, hsNormSq (q.toLinearIsometry.toContinuousLinearMap ∘L X ∘L q.symm.toLinearIsometry.toContinuousLinearMap) = hsNormSq X
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, notation paragraph ("its orthogonal projection (starProjection) is P_q(A) = q Pi(A) q^-1" and "Conjugation by a linear isometry preserves |.|"), used in steps 1, 3 and 4 of the parent proof.

Notation. N := n + l; Amb n l = EuclideanSpace R (Fin N); E_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 (k in Fin N) is the standard orthonormal basis; <.,.> is the inner product; hsNormSq Y = sum_k ||Y E_k||^2.

1. (a) Every subspace of the finite-dimensional space R^N is complete, so the orthogonal projections onto K and onto K.map q exist. Let z in R^N and u := q(p_K(q^(-1) z)). Then u lies in q(K) = K.map q. For every element q k of q(K) (k in K): <z - u, q k> = <q(q^(-1) z - p_K(q^(-1) z)), q k> = <q^(-1) z - p_K(q^(-1) z), k> = 0, because q preserves inner products and q^(-1) z - p_K(q^(-1) z) is orthogonal to K. By the characterization of the orthogonal projection (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero), the projection of z onto q(K) is u = (Q o p_K o Q') z. (This is Mathlib's Submodule.starProjection_map_apply.) As z is arbitrary, the two continuous linear maps are equal; formally ContinuousLinearMap.ext fun z => Submodule.starProjection_map_apply q K z closes (a) (a bare `ext z` would descend to EuclideanSpace coordinates, where the lemma no longer matches).

2. (b), transpose. For e in R^N define X^T e := sum_k <X E_k, e> E_k. For every u in R^N we have u = sum_k <E_k, u> E_k, so by linearity <X u, e> = sum_k <E_k, u> <X E_k, e> = <X^T e, u>.

3. Basis independence. Let (b_k)_(k in Fin N) be any orthonormal basis of R^N. Parseval's identity holds for both (E_j) and (b_k): ||z||^2 = sum_j <E_j, z>^2 = sum_k <b_k, z>^2 for every z (OrthonormalBasis.sum_sq_inner_right). Therefore
 sum_k ||X b_k||^2 = sum_k sum_j <E_j, X b_k>^2 = sum_j sum_k <X^T E_j, b_k>^2 = sum_j ||X^T E_j||^2,
 where the middle equality uses step 2 (<X b_k, E_j> = <X^T E_j, b_k>), the symmetry of the real inner product and the exchange of finite sums, and the last equality is Parseval for (b_k) applied to the vector X^T E_j. The right-hand side does not depend on the orthonormal basis (b_k).

4. Apply step 3 to b_k := q^(-1) E_k, an orthonormal basis since q^(-1) is a linear isometry equivalence (the image of the standard orthonormal basis, OrthonormalBasis.map), and to b_k := E_k. Using also that q is an isometry:
 hsNormSq (Q o X o Q') = sum_k ||q(X(q^(-1) E_k))||^2 = sum_k ||X(q^(-1) E_k)||^2 = sum_j ||X^T E_j||^2 = sum_k ||X E_k||^2 = hsNormSq X.
 This proves (b).
proof_key_steps: The projection onto q(K) is q o p_K o q^-1 (membership plus orthogonality characterization; starProjection_map_apply)
Hand-built transpose X^T e = sum_k <X E_k, e> E_k satisfies <X u, e> = <X^T e, u>
Parseval: sum_k ||X b_k||^2 = sum_j ||X^T E_j||^2 for every orthonormal basis (b_k)
Apply with b = q^-1 E and b = E; q is isometric, so hsNormSq (q X q^-1) = hsNormSq X

audit.reason: Both quantified clauses match the prose. Membership and orthogonality establish projection conjugation; the explicit transpose and Parseval calculation establish basis independence and hsNormSq invariance. Finite dimensionality supplies all projection instances, and composition has the intended meaning.
